newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian mergers rise in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Canadian mergers rise in third quarter.

text.p: The volume and value of Canadian mergers and acquisitions rose in the third quarter, although the value of announcements so far this year trailed that of 1995, said a report in Mergers & Acquisitions in Canada.

The publication by merchant bank Crosbie & Co. Inc., said the third-quarter dollar value of merger and acquisition announcements rose 7 percent to C$18.8 billion ($13.8 billion) from C$17.6 billion ($13 billion) a year ago.
The volume of mergers rose 28 percent to 328 transactions from 256 in the same period of 1995.
In the first nine months of this year, the value of announced mergers and acquisitions fell to C$53 billion ($39 billion) from C$66 billion ($56.4 billion) in the same period of 1995.

M&A in Canada said the decrease in the overall total was due mainly to the absence of some unusually large deals such as Seagram Co. Ltd.'s sale of its holding in DuPont Co. for C$12.2 billion ($9 billion) and Seagram's acquisition of MCA Inc. for C$7.8 billion ($5.7 billion).
Activity levels, however, rose 20 percent to 841 transactions from 704 in 1995.
M&A in Canada said the top industry sectors in dollar value of mergers and acquisitions were consumer products, oil and gas and transportation and environmental services.
